title: Organizational intelligence in action — with Anthropic | LIVESP129

segments.text: KARUANA GATIMU: I'm Karuana, and I can't be more excited
to be here with my friend from Anthropic.
We're going to show you some really cool stuff today.
I hope you're having a great time out there.
Big shout out to our digital audience who's been following
along from all over the world.
So, Max, tell everybody what you do.
Hey, how's it going?
MAX KIRBY: So I sit right where the breakthroughs
that we're making with our researchers meet actual
enterprise work.
So I have the pleasure of talking
to our most strategic customers
about what do you think we should do now, next,
maybe never, maybe wait to get started on things like that.
So exciting to be here.
The partnership between Microsoft
and Anthropic makes this conference so much fun for us.
I've seen so many interesting things that are being built,
and we're just excited to be here
and support everything going on.
KARUANA GATIMU: There's a lot of great energy here
in San Francisco, and this is a historic location here
in Fort Mason.
But tell me, this is your first Microsoft Build, I think.
Is that right?
MAX KIRBY: This is my first Microsoft Build.
Yeah.
KARUANA GATIMU: That's great.
Well, we're glad that you're here.
Tell us a little bit about the partnership
between our two companies.
I know it's deep and wide,
but help people understand how we're working together.
MAX KIRBY: Yeah.
So the way that we look at how we work with any kind of part
of the stack for an enterprise,
of which Microsoft has many different layers,
is there are certain areas that are going
to need the highest possible intelligence
for the transformation that is to come.
And then there are certain things that are infrastructure
that need to exist in order to make sure
that everything is working the way
that the enterprise needs it to work.
And then there are key things like identity, security,
and governance, of course, which are all part
of the same estate, usually.
So we try to make sure that Claude is able
to operate wherever the customer wants Claude.
And from the very beginning, we've taken a stance of, look,
however that needs to work for you, we're going to find a way
to make that available.
So I think the partnership,
at least from everything my team has been saying,
has been really successful in market so far,
and we're excited about what's next.
KARUANA GATIMU: Yeah.
That's absolutely true.
And of course, you hit on something.
When you're talking about intelligence,
we had announcements this morning about Microsoft IQ,
which extends the family of IQ experiences: Work IQ,
Foundry IQ, and Fabric IQ, with Web IQ.
And now these agents can actually operate and reason
across all of those domains of intelligence and information
to have a more impactful result.
Tell me how you think about that in terms of what you're building
and what you see enterprise customers really needing,
you know, because there's a whole conversation
about value going on and these agentic projects.
How do you all approach that?
MAX KIRBY: The transformation that is about to take reach
across the economy, across all the enterprises
where we're working together to help transform them,
requires something that we call legibility.
Legibility basically means
that AI can understand what's going on in a business.
Said another way, it's very hard for AI
to improve something that it cannot see.
And so, legibility we think is something
that every enterprise leader should be thinking about
and spending some thinking cycles on.
When we look at what's happening with Work IQ, especially,
the other IQ family now, we see that as a context layer
that can make more legibility, more interpretability
of what's happening
in a business available for AI to improve.
And this gives you two things.
The first thing is that it lets you know what's going on so
that you can actually see it.
If you ask most businesses,
"What are your standard operating procedures?"
they'll say, "Well, we have these documented,
but we don't actually know what all of the rest of them are."
KARUANA GATIMU: (Inaudible) is actually doing
to make something happen.
We call that the difference between the standard procedure
and the know-how that sometimes is in the humans in the process.
And so, yeah, there's no visibility there.
MAX KIRBY: We have a lot of empathy
for executive enterprise leaders who want
to make the right decisions,
make sure that everyone makes this transition safely,
but aren't necessarily as familiar with the people working
on boots on the ground, familiar with the problems
that they're running into on a day-to-day basis.
And I think all of the leaders that I've spoken to want
to be more in touch with those things, but it's the function
of documentation and processes, and this is what we mean
when we say legibility.
So if you can get there, then the second thing
that you can do, which I'm really excited about,
is you can observe what you should build in the first place.
And we think this is more like the future
of building technology, is observing first
so that then you can infer what should you build
in the first place, and that's a total flip
from how technology has been built the last 20 years.
KARUANA GATIMU: And that's directly impactful
on the community that we have here at Microsoft Build as well,
and plus all of us who want to make sure
that we're getting real value from the work
that we're doing in this space.
It's fantastic.
Now, I know you have a demo.
Let's play that demo.
MAX KIRBY: So we'll let this play in the background.
But what you're going to see is a set of experiments
that we're very excited about that are starting to work
when it comes to legibility and what Claude can do
to tell you what to build in the first place.
So what you just saw was lots of different AI tools,
Copilot as well as Claude, and we have an agent
in the system that's looking at every one
of those transcripts and those traces.
And so, you're seeing now on Foundry, that agent pulling
out different observations that are coming
from the real use of technology.
KARUANA GATIMU: I love this view.
I have to tell you how much I love this view because I've been
that person where the developers and the stakeholders
and the project managers,
they're not aligned on what to do next.
And you just showed me this beautiful way
of observing what actual people are doing.
Oh, and let's talk through this part.
MAX KIRBY: So this is where it gets really interesting.
There are two things that we've really put a lot of effort
into making Claude excellent at.
The first, which most people understand, is code,
specifically codebase comprehension,
or understanding how a codebase works, dependencies
between different files.
This is a major focus for us at Anthropic.
The second is user-centricity or empathy
from a human perspective.
And that gives Claude the ability to both empathize
with the users that it's observing running into problems,
suggesting features, or doing things
that might suggest features, and at the same time,
it can infer what code needs to change in order
to satisfy that need state.
Now, this makes possible something that is very different
in terms of how we build software.
Usually, you would build.
You'd operate.
Then you would put analytics on it,
and you'd say, "Is it working?
Is it being adopted?"
We're seeing now that model start to flip around.
We're actually able to observe first
to infer there what should we build based on what needs
to be actually in the operations.
So this is going to change how we look at technology
across the board, and I'm just so excited
to actually give builders the ability to say, "Well,
we're kind of having to guess about what would work,"
and now they're not going to have to guess.
They're going to be able to say, "These are the problems
that my users are running into.
What can I do to provide more value?"
And if you can keep running that loop and that cycle,
you're just creating tons more value for everybody.
KARUANA GATIMU: There's another reason --
first off, that's mind-blowing.
I love watching that work.
I think it's fantastic.
But there's another reason I think this is important,
and I'm sure you've thought about, which is making sure
that businesses are implementing AI in meaningful ways,
and growing the top line, using AI as a way to go further,
go faster, come up with new things.
For me, AI isn't about efficiencies and what have you,
though that can be one of the outcomes.
It's really about innovation and what you can do next.
And so, I feel like this helps builders
and developers have those conversations
with their stakeholders as they're thinking about where
to invest their time and resources.
MAX KIRBY: We completely agree.
This is why we think that high intelligence is so important.
Because if you can get the intelligence right,
there's an infinite demand for it, number one.
And number two is, if you think that you're limited
by your ability to create value for your customer,
intelligence will help you figure
out how can you remove those blockers in the first place.
So it's funny because I feel like very soon,
AI strategy will also involve just kind
of ask Claude what to do.
And that's a great outcome because that means
that we can also help people figure out what to do
in the first place and then how to get it right.
And I think a lot of leaders are struggling comparing those two
-- the problem space and the solution space --
and wondering which to focus on first.
Hopefully, we can finesse that problem.
KARUANA GATIMU: I also think you mentioned leaders
in that conversation, and I think that leaders and builders
and the people who manage them and invest in them need
to understand that this requires a certain degree of both courage
and a release of control.
Now, I do this every day.
I talk to my agents.
I talk to my Copilot experiences, and have them work
with me through problems and give me ideas and think
about how I should think about things.
But I feel like I've learned how to do that over the last couple
of years, and I've had to let go of the control
that I might always be right.
Do you see people doing that?
Do you see leaders leaning in to actually using AI in that way?
MAX KIRBY: Yes.
Some of the most meaningful moments working
with our enterprise customers are
when they understand the potential there.
And I'll give you one kind of piece of advice
that we've seen work pretty much across the board.
I mean, you could take the startups out of this,
but that's a little apples and oranges.
If you release a policy memo and say,
"This is what you're supposed to use AI for,
and this is what you're not supposed to use AI for,"
what works much better is having a non-technical senior leader
demo and show the organization, "This is what I use AI
for to inform my decisions, to try to do my job better."
That sort of openness and vulnerability,
it signals the right things.
And that's when we see these adoption numbers change.
And the human factors there can't be summarized
by what would be made more efficient because we want
to bring as many people with us on this transformation.
The problem is that unless you're actually using it
and getting in the reps and having those moments
where the penny drops and you go, "Wow,
I can ask it to ask me questions."
These are the things that we think more
and more people are going to be discovering as we roll
out these tools, and, of course, in partnership with Microsoft
for all the enterprises that we serve.
KARUANA GATIMU: Absolutely.
And we call that finding your aha moment
in the user adoption realm, and there's no replacement
for having somebody visibly learning
in front of other people.
It signals that proper cultural transformation
that actually precedes the Frontier Transformation
that we're always talking about, and the workforce one
that I talk about a lot myself.
So this is your first Microsoft Build,
and we have such a fantastic partnership together.
What are you excited that we're going to do together next?
MAX KIRBY: I think the legibility conversation has
required both of our organizations
to become more compatible with each other and also
to provide the value in the different pieces of the stack
that only we can uniquely provide.
And I think that's something
that we should double and triple down on.
In the beginning, when everyone started to use AI
in their personal lives, I don't know about you,
but I wore out the copy and paste button on my keyboard.
We were just constantly moving context
from one thing to another.
And then we entered the tool-calling era
with Anthropic's release of MCP.
And now we're starting to get to the point
where once you can get all of the information
that is describing the work that's happening,
you can really root cause analysis all
of these opportunities to improve it.
That, I think, should be our North Star together.
KARUANA GATIMU: That is fantastic.
I'm so inspired by the work that's happening at Anthropic
and across this space at large, and I know that all
of you probably are as well.
There's a lot of fantastic demos, including a deeper dive
in the one that we showed today on the showcase page,
the sponsor page that you have.
And I think everybody should go check it
out because you're going to want to follow along and make sure
that you understand how to have this conversation
in the enterprise with the developers and the builders
that you have and how to just dig
in right now and get things going.
That's very important.
Like, get your hands on the keyboard, test these things out,
make sure you understand, and then come back
to our communities and have the conversation with other builders
who are doing this work because we're all in this together.
I firmly believe that AI is a team sport,
and we have to do this together for it
to have the greatest benefits.
MAX KIRBY: Absolutely.
KARUANA GATIMU: So I am really excited that you're here.
Thank you so much.
And thanks to everyone who's following along.
We'll see you again soon.
MAX KIRBY: Bye.
